Kento Alpha 0.9.36, build 2922

New

  • File > Add to this comp... brings another comp's nodes (a .nk or a .ko) into the comp in front, beside what's there, as one undo. The open comp keeps its own range, format and frame rate, and says where the added comp's differed; footage paths are made absolute so they still find their files.
  • Copy and paste with Nuke and between Kento windows. Copy puts the selected nodes on the system clipboard as Nuke script text and as Kento's own copy; Paste reads nodes copied in Nuke, or in another Kento, with Kento's readers.
  • Python in comps and gizmos runs, as in Nuke. A gizmo's onCreate, its knobChanged as its panel opens and whenever a control changes, and its Python buttons all run, through Kento's stand-in for Nuke's Python module; what a control's change does through its script comes off with it in one undo. A gizmo whose script rebuilds its inside when a control changes does so here too, and its text lines, dividers and buttons hide and dim as its script says.
  • A comp's own callbacks run: onScriptLoad as a Nuke script opens, onScriptSave before it's saved as one, and the comp's and each Write's before and after render and frame callbacks in the Render window, the Render Queue and command-line renders.
  • Before any script runs, Kento reads it. One that reaches files, the shell or the network still runs, and a card in the window's corner shows the lines and why. Don't warn about this script again trusts it from then on. Settings > Scripting can ask before such a script runs instead (off by default).
  • Scripts can read bounding boxes (a node's bbox, as in Nuke), run a CurveTool's analysis, and use Nuke's AutoCrop, which keys a Crop to the picture over the comp's range.
  • Kento's own Python module for scripts, tools and batches: import kento in the Script Editor, a startup script or Kento's Python without the interface. Comps, nodes and knobs by Nuke's names, keys at frames, one undo for a block of changes; every remote control command from a script; the Viewer (show a node, its look, its wipe); callbacks when comps open and close, the frame changes or nodes are added; and a stub file so code editors complete the calls.
  • Kiri's Balance: Match to background sets exposure, contrast, warmth and tint part of the way toward the plate behind, each with a lock, and light wrap brings the background's light around the edges.
  • Kiri's checking views, in its row over the Viewer: Result, Matte, Bands, Spill and Foreground.
  • Kiri's kept colors: pick colors the despill leaves alone (a green costume, a plant) with the dropper; a pixel near a kept color keeps its own color at any brightness.

Fixes

  • Setting a box control from a script with four numbers set both corners to the first number.
  • A gizmo's scripts read as written in the Nuke script: before, they could look as if they had nothing to do.

Kento Alpha 0.9.35, build 2909

New

  • Kiri, Kento's own keyer (Keyer, Kiri). It does the screen key, three mattes, despill and the foreground over the background in one node. Choose Green, Blue or Auto in its header, and press Auto to find the screen's color. Core, edge and garbage mattes come from the key or from a matte input, each grown or shrunk and softened. Click the subject puts an Isolate under the plate, and its mask becomes the core and the garbage. Smart despill is chosen by the screen: on green, green is limited to 0.6 red + 0.4 blue, the best of the methods tried on the studio's greenscreen tests. The mattes and the spill can be written as channels of their own.
  • Without a clean plate, Kiri finds the screen in the plate by its color rather than its brightness, so a screen lit unevenly, overexposed, or seen through tinted glass keys evenly. On a car interior shot through a moon roof, the screen behind the tinted glass keyed clear, leaving the glass's reflections over the new background.
  • Kiri unmixes edges from the screen behind them before the despill, which takes the light fringe off edges against a bright screen, and puts the spill's brightness back as light (the new background's or gray), so spilled skin doesn't go dull.
  • Kiri can key from a degrained copy of the plate, so the grain doesn't chatter in the matte, while the foreground keeps the plate's own grain. Make one with Nagi builds the copy. On the moon roof shot it halved the matte's noise behind the glass.
  • Still to come in Kiri, drawn in its panel and saying so: the edge refinement by a matting model, steadiness over frames, kept colors, and the Balance section.
  • Perspective's Match to has a fourth choice, Horizon and forward point (Transform), for a background behind a foreground shot elsewhere, such as a road plate behind a car interior. Each plate needs only lines along its ground's forward direction, a road's edges for instance, and no focal length. The other plate is moved so the points those lines meet at line up, turned to this plate's horizon, and the box says how much of the frame is left uncovered at the top.
  • Perspective's Match to can match two plates by their pictures (From the pictures): the other plate's pixels are fitted onto this one's, with no lines needed. On the studio's plates it lands within a fraction of a pixel.
  • Find lines names each edge's direction itself, before anything is solved: the edges are drawn in their direction's color. Click one to add it, or Shift-click to add every edge of that color.
  • VectorGenerator can write a confidence channel: how far each vector can be trusted, from the forward and backward vectors agreeing and the next frame matching. VectorRetime and FlowRetime can blend the frames instead of warping where the vectors are unsure, so a fast object's edges don't tear.
  • The Lens node has 3DE's Anamorphic, degree 6 and Radial fisheye, degree 8 models, matching LensDistortion2's presets.

Fixes

  • Find lines finds the edges on scene-linear plates. A few bright lights left every other edge too faint: on one studio plate of a street with towers it found 2 lines, now over a hundred.
  • Perspective's Horizon only match turns the other plate the right way, about its horizon. A plate of another size gets its own corners in Full perspective.
  • Perspective's Match to says when either plate's focal length is uncertain, and points to From the pictures.
  • The lens from lines warns when the distortion it found is more than a lens that long would show.

Kento Alpha 0.9.34, build 2885

Speed

  • Colorspace works each pixel's color out once for its red, green and blue, where it had worked it out once for each channel. Comps with many Colorspace nodes, such as layers blended in their own color space, render faster: on one studio comp Colorspace took half the time.
  • FilterErode with the Box filter costs the same at any size. At large sizes it is many times faster: a size of 200 took about 2 seconds a frame and now takes a few hundredths. One studio comp's frame went from 5.1 to 2.9 seconds.
  • Both give exactly the same pixels as before, checked against every Write of five studio comps.
